description: Less talk. More work. Greater impact.
summary: Flame in Freefall is an AI-powered platform that makes NASA and JAXA microgravity combustion experiments easier to explore and understand. It transforms experimental data into a structured, queryable knowledge base and allows users to ask natural-language questions about flame behavior, combustion conditions, and fire-safety measurements. Using a structured-first RAG architecture, the system retrieves deterministic numerical results through DuckDB and generates evidence-based answers with verified citations. By reducing the effort required to search and compare complex experimental records, Flame in Freefall helps researchers access reliable scientific evidence and better understand fire behavior in microgravity. This supports improved fire-risk assessment and safety planning for future spacecraft, space stations, and lunar or Martian habitats.
details:
Flame in Freefall is an AI-powered platform designed to make microgravity combustion research easier to explore and understand. Users can ask natural-language questions about experimental conditions, flame behavior, and fire-safety measurements. The system converts questions into structured query plans, retrieves numerical results from experimental datasets using DuckDB, and generates evidence-based explanations with verified citations.

The project helps researchers search, compare, and interpret complex experimental records more efficiently. Its intended impact is to support a better understanding of fire behavior in microgravity and contribute to fire-safety planning for future spacecraft, space stations, and lunar or Martian habitats.

We developed the platform using Python, FastAPI, React, TypeScript, and Vite. Data processing and querying rely on Pandas, PyArrow, and DuckDB. We also integrated Groq API with GPT-OSS-20B for natural-language query planning and answer generation, with Qdrant and FastEmbed for optional semantic retrieval.

The creative aspect is its structured-first RAG approach: instead of relying on an LLM to invent numerical answers, the system retrieves measurements deterministically and grounds explanations in verifiable experimental evidence. Our team considered data reliability, traceability, usability, and the need to make scientific information accessible without sacrificing accuracy.
